item.content:encoded:
This fell flat for me. The note at the beginning reads like one of those "not quite over lol!foundation, so we're going to have a pointless snarky comment from the researcher" bits that crop up in articles from this era, altered broadcasts aren't that unique in and of themselves, the 2spuppy monologue came out as goofy, and without any investment in or context for He-Who-Made-Light/Dark, I didn't really care that much.

Also, the last paragraph could benefit from some line breaks.

Also, "door, not window," combined with the fact that you need to insert an anomalous object into and then turn on the television set for anomalies to manifest, fails to really be that scary. It reminds me a bit of the premise of the Holders, where the unspeakable horror of the ritual is undercut by the fact that you could just not do the ritual.

This is near 200, so it's obviously something folks like, but it's definitely not for me. -1

I know this is a gravedig, but…

The tubes are only even POTENTIALLY dangerous when installed. If they're that intert when not used, and there seems to be no intelligence gleaned from using the SCP, unplug them, store them in 8 boxes a long way from each other, and lock them down.

Keeping them together, much less installed in a 719-compatible unit, only makes sense if there's something to be gained from the SCP.

This is more than a nitpick, it's nearly LOLFoundation levels of silly/inept. There needs to be either a benefit to turning it on, or a penalty for NOT turning it on.

item.content:encoded:
In my head-cannon, if an SCP causes something else to behave anomalously, the "something else" often gets an SCP designation of its own while it's behaving anomalously. Lots of examples of people interacting with SCP-XXX and becoming SCP-XXX-1 and so on. That's the reasoning, anyway. The TV was SCP-719, rather than the tubes, because I think the foundation identified the whole unit as an SCP before they discovered they could swap the tubes out with another TV. By that time, I don't think anyone saw a pressing need to change the nomenclature (in fact, I see a reasonable policy of resisting that sort of thing. What someone misses a documentation update?)

As for storage, as long as no power's going to the TV, they haven't noticed any anomalous behavior. So I don't see them having any reason not to treat it as a unit.

I up-voted, now let me nit-pick. Neither of these seriously hurts the article, but they are dings in my opinion

The TV is not anomalous, the crystals are. The TV is just an activation condition for the anomaly and shouldn't get a designation number all to itself.

Why are the crystals stored in a TV? I don't see any negative effects from unhooking them. It would be safer to keep the crystals unplugged. That way you would have no chance of accidental activation or any unforseen secondary effects from long-term connection.

item.content:encoded:
I too greatly enjoy video and broadcast-style SCPs, and for that reason (in addition to the fact that it's executed well) I am giving this an upvote. However, I have a couple of nitpicks:

Addendum to Containment Procedures ██/██/20██: From this point forward, stop testing this thing on D-class subjects. We’ve wasted a dozen so far, and the only anomalous effect on them has been radiation poisoning. —O5-█

This may be thing where I'm just trying to force my own headcanon, but I don't see why an O5 would get directly involved in something like that. This is a Safe-class object which, while lethal and disturbing, doesn't seem to represent an especially dire threat in relation to other SCPs, and I would think that the Research Director or perhaps even a Site Director would take care of this issue.

When SCP-719-1 is in place, and SCP-719 is supplied power and turned on, SCP-719-1 will radiate electromagnetic radiation in various spectra including visible light, ultraviolet, [REDACTED], [REDACTED] and a substantial band in [REDACTED]. About 60% of emissions are ionizing radiation.

I have no idea what you're doing with the redactions here. Are there classified portions of the electromagnetic spectrum now or something? This, to me, was a dissonant note in an otherwise well-written article.

On the more positive side, I kind of like the fact that it's a "Satanic" cult, but not like some cheesy horror-movie style one.

Also:

■External scenes will gradually become brighter, night becomes day, clouds vanish, and the sun— when visible— will grow progressively larger and whiter.

I don't know what your Photoshop skillz are like (mine are nonexistent or I would attempt it myself), but a picture in the article depicting this stage of the broadcast, IMHO, would look extremely badass and add a lot to the article.

Overall, good work.
